# Knowledge map: L2 full-system kernel boot (UnicornMachine)

<!-- Generated by `python -m tools.research.knowledge_map build` from `docs/map/sources/l2-kernel-boot.toml`. Do not edit by hand. -->

- **Scope:** Booting the original CXD90045 Linux 3.0.27 updater and main kernels under UnicornMachine: EXBL/ATAGS/kemco, timer/GIC/UART, MMU and exception delivery, Thumb user continuation, nflasha3 main-firmware boot and QEMU-oracle peripherals.
- **Evidence span:** see record index; last reviewed 2026-11-22.
- **Deep review:** 88 of 88 records read in full and checked claim by claim ([curation plan](CURATION_PLAN.md)); the rest are curated from titles, lead paragraphs and consolidated documents.
- **Status legend:** PHYSICAL = observed on the camera/host; OFFLINE = disassembly, Unicorn or static proof; INFERENCE = argued from evidence, not observed directly; RETRACTED/REFUTED = do not rely on, kept to prevent re-derivation.

The evidence records are authoritative; follow the links before acting on a claim.

## Entities

### <a id="tool-unicorn-machine"></a>UnicornMachine (L2 full-system executor)

`tool.unicorn-machine` | tool

Full-system Unicorn machine booting original CXD90045 Linux 3.0.27 kernels with explicit peripheral models; single-core Cortex-A9 execution.

Current knowledge:

- **C07** `OFFLINE` The offline nflasha1 updater kernel boots to an interactive BusyBox v1.13.4 /bin/ash on ttyAM0 and runs uname -a and ls -la / (800M instructions, 11,420 serial bytes, no unmapped access). It needed amba2.console=1 with PL011 IRQ 150 delivery, kuser-page hooks and COW decode at 0xFFFF0FCC, a SoftMMU flush on switch_mm, and per-frame SP_usr restore so a sys_clone child keeps its own stack. This run still used the manual-restore machinery later removed by E0533. ([E0510](../evidence/0510-nflasha1-busybox-ash-ttyam0-shell.md))
- **C09** `OFFLINE` Unicorn and the patched QEMU sony-a6400 board match in the ret_to_user window except CPSR.A (QEMU sets it on kernel entry and IRQ entry) and F; non-secure A/F handling reproduces the exception return. Unicorn runs as Cortex-A9 (MIDR 0x410FC090) and QEMU as Cortex-A5 (0x410FC051), so adjacent proc_info slots are chosen; the first user Thumb entry address differs between runs (historical 0x0402E790, later 0x0400C790 / 0x040C2790); the Thumb loader prefix matches while the VFP capability word differs. ([E0545](../evidence/0545-unicorn-qemu-return-window-cpsr-a.md), [E0547](../evidence/0547-blocker-probe-kernel-entry-and-user-bytes.md), [E0548](../evidence/0548-head-stub-registers-die-before-v7-setup.md), [E0558](../evidence/0558-unicorn-qemu-kernel-entry-async-abort-mask.md), [E0559](../evidence/0559-unicorn-qemu-irq-async-abort-mask.md), [E0560](../evidence/0560-unicorn-nonsecure-af-exception-return.md), [E0562](../evidence/0562-thumb-loader-stack-vfp-capability.md))
- **C10** `OFFLINE` The updater child/COW continuation works after making the handle_mm_fault return hook passive; with --vfp-d16-mvfr0 the kernel advertises AT_HWCAP 0x0000E0D7, matching QEMU. ([E0653](../evidence/0653-unicorn-updater-child-cow-and-hwcap.md))
- **C11** `OFFLINE` Captured nflasha3 main firmware boots under UnicornMachine through stock /sbin/init, 9 mounts, 39 .ko modules, LIRO entry_main, im.elf DMP_2D_Initialize : 0 and /bin/ash past 2.8B instructions under --mmio stop. ([E0656](../evidence/0656-unicorn-main-firmware-boot.md))
- **C12** `OFFLINE` Opt-in --qemu-peripherals add the QEMU SYSV/VPH/evsel frame clock (SYSV 0xF3402000 IRQ 98 every 33,367 us, VPH 60 Hz vsync IRQ 101/102, evsel ext-vd IRQ 83/84) and QEMU-oracle SIO channel-3 start/done (IRQ 204), GPIO port-1 input 0x32 and ADC done with released-key results 0x3FF. These models are unit-tested; no captured nflasha3 replay was run with them, and the E0656 input set is not in this workspace. ([E0676](../evidence/0676-unicorn-sysv-vph-frame-clock.md), [E0677](../evidence/0677-unicorn-sio-gpio-oracle.md))
- **C13** `OFFLINE` No ld.so.preload, ld.so.conf, init.d or rcS ships in the live or packaged initrd or in /usr; preload paths are debug modes gated by /setting/mode/dmode and /setting/mode/preload. im.elf's environment has no LD_PRELOAD or LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Runtime /etc is a writable vfat mount of /dev/nflasha10, where /etc/ld.so.preload lists only the two project-installed diagnostics. The init mount table and order were recovered. ([E0418](../evidence/0418b-userspace-ld-preload-and-runtime-mounts.md))
- **C24** `OFFLINE` A later return-window probe restores the stopped QEMU VM, and the blocker probe reads kernel-entry CPSR and the user instruction. ([E0546](../evidence/0546-qemu-return-window-checkpoint-restores.md), [E0547](../evidence/0547-blocker-probe-kernel-entry-and-user-bytes.md))
- **C34** `OFFLINE` The kernel's klog buffer (klog.addr=0x034A0000, 128 KiB) holds the real boot log. It shows console [klog0] as the only console (so nothing went to the PL011), a CRCDC timeout at 0xF2A31000, dwc3 probe -110, the cramfs root mounted read-only and then 'Failed to execute /sbin/init ... Kernel panic - not syncing: No init found' followed by Sony's exception monitor. UART0..2 resources are 0xF2000000/0xF2001000/0xF2002000. ([E0421](../evidence/0421-cxd90045-ttyam0-uart-and-cramfs-init-boot.md), [E0422](../evidence/0422-cxd90045-pl011-membase-and-userspace-init.md))
- **C40** `OFFLINE` Kernel VAs (0x60000000+) were written through Unicorn's physical mem_read/mem_write without translation, corrupting pt_regs; translating them fixed ARM_sp. The secondary crash at do_page_fault+0x34 was a NULL thread_info->task on a stale captured SVC stack (0x7DC0C000 instead of 0x7DC0E000); using the live banked SP_svc and refreshing it at ret_to_user gives a valid task (0x7E36DBE0). A same-fault guard (8 repeats) cut diagnostic runs to about 16 s. ([E0437](../evidence/0437-cxd90045-page-fault-pt-regs-and-live-ash.md), [E0439](../evidence/0439-cxd90045-mm-fault-fix-swi-and-live-ash.md), [E0440](../evidence/0440-cxd90045-svc-stack-refresh-and-live-ash.md), [E0441](../evidence/0441-cxd90045-loop-guard-stack-trace-and-ash.md))
- **C43** `OFFLINE` TTBR1 reads live as 0x00104000 (swapper_pg_dir) and the vmalloc/fixmap walk was fixed. Running the whole boot under the virtual TLB then hit __rt_mutex_init(NULL) from a separate init_section_page_cgroup invocation (647 normal iterations carry valid heap pointers), so the virtual TLB is now switched on only at the first user return; the early boot stays on UC_TLB_CPU. ([E0449](../evidence/0449-cxd90045-ttbr1-fixmap-and-live-ash.md), [E0450](../evidence/0450-cxd90045-rt-mutex-caller-and-live-ash.md), [E0451](../evidence/0451-cxd90045-page-cgroup-vmalloc-and-ash.md), [E0452](../evidence/0452-cxd90045-deferred-virtual-tlb-and-live-ash.md))

### <a id="boot-contract"></a>Boot contract: EXBL, machine ID, ATAGS and kemco override

`boot.contract` | process | inventory `kernel.text:setup_arch`

Raw kernel at PA 0x00108000 / VA 0x60108000, machine ID 0xDA9, initrd at 0x00700000, boot params at 0x00103000; setup_arch requires a 'kemco' override payload; nflashaB0 holds an EXBL container loading DGU5.

Aliases: `0x00000DA9`, `ARM-CXD900X0`, `kemco`, `0x00103000`, `DGU5`

Current knowledge:

- **C01** `OFFLINE` nflasha1 holds a complete updater boot set (ARM zImage, cramfs initrd, kemco.txt with console=ttyAM0,115200n8, loadaddr.txt 0x00108000/0x00700000/0x00103000, p1chksum MD5s of the two images); nflasha3 holds the main set. The app requests an update by writing /setting/updater/mode* markers and running ud_send_lsi.elf / ud_reboot.elf; the updater consumes mode1/2/3/5/6. The loader-to-Linux boot mode is backup record 0x51000F (UPDATER 3, ADJUST 5, USB_CHARGE 6, BIS 0x0C), read by upm.ko and bootin.elf. ([E0413](../evidence/0413-cxd90045-updater-mode-offline-analysis.md))
- **C02** `OFFLINE` Sony's setup_arch accepts a boot-parameter override at 0x60103000 only if it starts with 'kemco' (strncmp 5); it then parses from ptr+5, turns CR/LF into spaces and stops at '*'. Standard ATAGS or raw cmdline text there are rejected ('invalid cmdline override') and the built-in kemco CONFIG_CMDLINE (init=/sbin/init) is used. With the kemco form, init=/bin/ash is parsed and attempted. ([E0424](../evidence/0424-cxd90045-pl011-primecell-and-ash-shell.md), [E0425](../evidence/0425-cxd90045-cmdline-override-and-interactive-ash.md))
- **C07** `OFFLINE` The offline nflasha1 updater kernel boots to an interactive BusyBox v1.13.4 /bin/ash on ttyAM0 and runs uname -a and ls -la / (800M instructions, 11,420 serial bytes, no unmapped access). It needed amba2.console=1 with PL011 IRQ 150 delivery, kuser-page hooks and COW decode at 0xFFFF0FCC, a SoftMMU flush on switch_mm, and per-frame SP_usr restore so a sys_clone child keeps its own stack. This run still used the manual-restore machinery later removed by E0533. ([E0510](../evidence/0510-nflasha1-busybox-ash-ttyam0-shell.md))
- **C14** `OFFLINE` A PL011 alias with bidirectional UART and the PID-1 panic root cause moved the updater boot on to /sbin/init diagnosis. ([E0422](../evidence/0422-cxd90045-pl011-membase-and-userspace-init.md))
- **C25** `OFFLINE` The updater cramfs /sbin/init loads its modules, mounts /setting, starts UdtrMain.sh and then loops a password-less /bin/ash --login on the console unless /root/IAMLDUDWRT exists (it does not in the preserved image). viewUnified2.so has DT_NEEDED CautionConfig.so, so a truncated CautionConfig.so stops the unified UI at link time. ([E0413](../evidence/0413-cxd90045-updater-mode-offline-analysis.md))
- **C26** `PHYSICAL` In normal boot nflashaB0, nflashaB1, nflasha1 and nflasha3 are readable with O_RDONLY (not locked after boot); read-only dumps were streamed through the debugger and re-hashed on the host. nflashaB0 starts with EXBL and carries loader code; nflashaB1 is all zero (zeroed vs zero-backed is unknown); nflasha1 matches the E0306 dump byte for byte. ([E0414](../evidence/0414-nflasha-readonly-device-check-and-boot-area-dumps.md))
- **C27** `OFFLINE` nflashaB0 is the first-stage loader: one 0x200-byte EXBL container (seven 0x40-byte records, six used, load = 0xFE040000 + start*512, entry 0xFE047000 reset vector) holding a Sony DGU5 loader V85.00.03 with LPDDR3 init, FAT access, the 0x0051000F boot-mode literal, a backslash \updater\mode path and Backup.bin load strings. In Unicorn it programs UART0, clocks and the timer but never touches the 0x00103000 parameter block in the traced prefix. ([E0415](../evidence/0415-nflasha-boot-decode-and-full-emulation-roadmap.md), [E0416](../evidence/0416-cxd90045-qemu-updater-bringup.md))
- **C28** `OFFLINE` The live nflasha3 kernel, initrd and av-cam.bin differ from the update package (live Sony CE Linux 8.2.6.0, 2021; package 8.2.5.7, 2017); the other ten files are identical. The live dump is the authoritative input. Kernel layout: PA 0x00108000, PAGE_OFFSET 0x60000000, _stext 0x60108160, _etext 0x6048D024, linux_banner 0x603C8028, 24,600 symbols. ([E0415](../evidence/0415-nflasha-boot-decode-and-full-emulation-roadmap.md))
- **C29** `OFFLINE` Machine ID 0x0DA9 (ARM-CXD900X0) was recovered from both kernels' machine_desc. With a reconstructed 884-byte ATAG list at 0x00103000 (core, two memory banks, cmdline) and r0=0, r1=0x0DA9, r2=0x00103000, the updater kernel runs head.S, enables the MMU and reaches calibrate_delay, which waits for a timer interrupt. GIC distributor 0xF8001000, CPU interface 0xF8000100 and timer 0xF2403000 were recovered from the init code. ([E0416](../evidence/0416-cxd90045-qemu-updater-bringup.md))
- **C32** `OPEN` Contradiction to resolve: E0413 lists /sbin/init (a shell script) among the updater cramfs entries, while the E0422/E0425 cramfs decodes of nflasha1 boot/initrd.img find no /sbin/init or /bin/sh, and the default boot panics with 'Failed to execute /sbin/init ... No init found'. Later boots use init=/bin/ash. ([E0413](../evidence/0413-cxd90045-updater-mode-offline-analysis.md), [E0422](../evidence/0422-cxd90045-pl011-membase-and-userspace-init.md), [E0425](../evidence/0425-cxd90045-cmdline-override-and-interactive-ash.md))
- **C34** `OFFLINE` The kernel's klog buffer (klog.addr=0x034A0000, 128 KiB) holds the real boot log. It shows console [klog0] as the only console (so nothing went to the PL011), a CRCDC timeout at 0xF2A31000, dwc3 probe -110, the cramfs root mounted read-only and then 'Failed to execute /sbin/init ... Kernel panic - not syncing: No init found' followed by Sony's exception monitor. UART0..2 resources are 0xF2000000/0xF2001000/0xF2002000. ([E0421](../evidence/0421-cxd90045-ttyam0-uart-and-cramfs-init-boot.md), [E0422](../evidence/0422-cxd90045-pl011-membase-and-userspace-init.md))

Do not rely on:

- ~~The first-stage loader is not preserved anywhere, and no updater-mode path exists outside /setting.~~ **R02** `RETRACTED` ([E0413](../evidence/0413-cxd90045-updater-mode-offline-analysis.md)); see C27: nflashaB0 is the first-stage loader: one 0x200-byte EXBL container (seven 0x40-byte records, six used, load = 0xFE040000 + start*512, entry 0xFE047000 reset vector) holding a Sony DGU5 loader V85.00.03 with LPDDR3 init, FAT access, the 0x0051000F boot-mode literal, a backslash \updater\mode path and Backup.bin load strings. In Unicorn it programs UART0, clocks and the timer but never touches the 0x00103000 parameter block in the traced prefix.
- ~~nflashaB0 holds a second EXBL record at offset 0xCDE0.~~ **R03** `RETRACTED` ([E0414](../evidence/0414-nflasha-readonly-device-check-and-boot-area-dumps.md)); see C27: nflashaB0 is the first-stage loader: one 0x200-byte EXBL container (seven 0x40-byte records, six used, load = 0xFE040000 + start*512, entry 0xFE047000 reset vector) holding a Sony DGU5 loader V85.00.03 with LPDDR3 init, FAT access, the 0x0051000F boot-mode literal, a backslash \updater\mode path and Backup.bin load strings. In Unicorn it programs UART0, clocks and the timer but never touches the 0x00103000 parameter block in the traced prefix. *Note: E0415: 0xCDE0 lies inside loader segment 0 (an EXBL literal in its string data), not a second container.*

### <a id="soc-irq-timer-uart"></a>GIC, timer, PL011 UART and CRCDC clock

`soc.irq-timer-uart` | device

GICv1 distributor 0xF8001000 / CPU interface 0xF8000100, timer 0xF2403000 (IRQ 153, 100 Hz), PL011 UART0 ttyAM0 at 0xF2000000, CRCDC clock 0xF2A31000.

Aliases: `0xF8001000`, `0xF2403000`, `0xF2000000`, `ttyAM0`, `0xF2A31000`

Current knowledge:

- **C02** `OFFLINE` Sony's setup_arch accepts a boot-parameter override at 0x60103000 only if it starts with 'kemco' (strncmp 5); it then parses from ptr+5, turns CR/LF into spaces and stops at '*'. Standard ATAGS or raw cmdline text there are rejected ('invalid cmdline override') and the built-in kemco CONFIG_CMDLINE (init=/sbin/init) is used. With the kemco form, init=/bin/ash is parsed and attempted. ([E0424](../evidence/0424-cxd90045-pl011-primecell-and-ash-shell.md), [E0425](../evidence/0425-cxd90045-cmdline-override-and-interactive-ash.md))
- **C12** `OFFLINE` Opt-in --qemu-peripherals add the QEMU SYSV/VPH/evsel frame clock (SYSV 0xF3402000 IRQ 98 every 33,367 us, VPH 60 Hz vsync IRQ 101/102, evsel ext-vd IRQ 83/84) and QEMU-oracle SIO channel-3 start/done (IRQ 204), GPIO port-1 input 0x32 and ADC done with released-key results 0x3FF. These models are unit-tested; no captured nflasha3 replay was run with them, and the E0656 input set is not in this workspace. ([E0676](../evidence/0676-unicorn-sysv-vph-frame-clock.md), [E0677](../evidence/0677-unicorn-sio-gpio-oracle.md))
- **C14** `OFFLINE` A PL011 alias with bidirectional UART and the PID-1 panic root cause moved the updater boot on to /sbin/init diagnosis. ([E0422](../evidence/0422-cxd90045-pl011-membase-and-userspace-init.md))
- **C29** `OFFLINE` Machine ID 0x0DA9 (ARM-CXD900X0) was recovered from both kernels' machine_desc. With a reconstructed 884-byte ATAG list at 0x00103000 (core, two memory banks, cmdline) and r0=0, r1=0x0DA9, r2=0x00103000, the updater kernel runs head.S, enables the MMU and reaches calibrate_delay, which waits for a timer interrupt. GIC distributor 0xF8001000, CPU interface 0xF8000100 and timer 0xF2403000 were recovered from the init code. ([E0416](../evidence/0416-cxd90045-qemu-updater-bringup.md))
- **C30** `OFFLINE` The CXD timer uses IRQ 153 (setup_irq 0x99) with gic_init(0, 29, 0xF8001000, 0xF8000100); timer base 0xF2403000: control +0x00, divider +0x04 (write 1 acknowledges), period +0x08 (0x2710 = 100 Hz on 1 MHz), free-running counter +0x10C. A GIC model with GICD_TYPER = 1024 lines delivered 368 timer IRQs, so calibrate_delay completes from real jiffies and the kernel reaches PCI, initrd probe and hwtimer init. ([E0417](../evidence/0417-cxd90045-timer-gic-and-ttyam0-boot.md))
- **C35** `OFFLINE` Two models unlocked the serial console: the CRCDC clock block (write 1 to 0xF2A31000+0x30, poll bit 0 clear) removes the timeout, and the PL011 PrimeCell ID registers (PeriphID 0x00141011, PCellID 0xB105F00D at +0xFE0..0xFFC) let amba_device_register succeed. Then 'uart0: ttyAM0 at MMIO 0xf2000000 (irq = 150)' and console [ttyAM0] enabled; 52,976 bytes were captured and injected RX bytes drive Sony's exception monitor, whose shell is compiled out (EM_DEBUG). ([E0423](../evidence/0423-cxd90045-crcdc-clock-and-ash-shell.md), [E0424](../evidence/0424-cxd90045-pl011-primecell-and-ash-shell.md))

Do not rely on:

- ~~The kernel's PL011 console uses a different physical base or an unobserved alias, which is why no UART writes appear at 0xF2000000.~~ **R06** `RETRACTED` ([E0420](../evidence/0420-cxd90045-ex-table-fixup-and-ttyam0-boot.md), [E0421](../evidence/0421-cxd90045-ttyam0-uart-and-cramfs-init-boot.md)); see C35: Two models unlocked the serial console: the CRCDC clock block (write 1 to 0xF2A31000+0x30, poll bit 0 clear) removes the timeout, and the PL011 PrimeCell ID registers (PeriphID 0x00141011, PCellID 0xB105F00D at +0xFE0..0xFFC) let amba_device_register succeed. Then 'uart0: ttyAM0 at MMIO 0xf2000000 (irq = 150)' and console [ttyAM0] enabled; 52,976 bytes were captured and injected RX bytes drive Sony's exception monitor, whose shell is compiled out (EM_DEBUG).

### <a id="mmu-exceptions"></a>MMU, virtual TLB and ARMv7 exception delivery

`mmu.exceptions` | process | inventory `kernel.text:do_page_fault`, `kernel.text:handle_mm_fault`, `kernel.text:__dabt_svc`, `kernel.text:__pabt_svc`, `kernel.text:cpu_v7_switch_mm`, `kernel.text:vector_swi`, `kernel.text:init_section_page_cgroup`

Deferred UC_TLB_VIRTUAL with a TLB-fill hook walking TTBR1/TTBR0, CP15 fault-register hooks, SWI/prefetch/data-abort re-dispatch and kuser helpers.

Aliases: `UC_TLB_VIRTUAL`, `UC_HOOK_TLB_FILL`, `DFAR`, `IFAR`

Current knowledge:

- **C03** `OFFLINE` Guest data aborts, __ex_table fixups, prefetch aborts, SP banking, CP15 IFSR/IFAR hooks and SVC-mode abort stubs were implemented step by step until real USER-mode execution ran. ([E0419](../evidence/0419-cxd90045-data-abort-and-ttyam0-boot.md), [E0420](../evidence/0420-cxd90045-ex-table-fixup-and-ttyam0-boot.md), [E0429](../evidence/0429-cxd90045-prefetch-abort-and-interactive-ash.md), [E0430](../evidence/0430-cxd90045-abt-sp-isolation-and-live-ash.md), [E0431](../evidence/0431-cxd90045-banked-usr-regs-and-live-ash.md), [E0433](../evidence/0433-cxd90045-pabt-mrc-hook-and-live-ash.md), [E0435](../evidence/0435-cxd90045-svc-vector-stub-and-live-ash.md))
- **C04** `OFFLINE` Two different translation problems blocked ld.so: the repeated 0x04031AF0 fault was a stale DFAR/DFSR on the user data-abort path (fixed, page installed), and the following 0x0402F666 loop persisted with a valid PTE because the guest's TLBIALL/TTBR0 maintenance does not flush Unicorn's SoftMMU. UC_TLB_VIRTUAL with a UC_HOOK_TLB_FILL page-table walker, a live-TTBR1 kernel walk and activation deferred to the first real user return resolve translation. ([E0441](../evidence/0441-cxd90045-loop-guard-stack-trace-and-ash.md), [E0443](../evidence/0443-cxd90045-04031af0-cpu-exception-and-ash.md), [E0445](../evidence/0445-cxd90045-cputlb-flush-and-live-ash.md), [E0446](../evidence/0446-cxd90045-pabt-cputlb-swi-and-live-ash.md), [E0448](../evidence/0448-cxd90045-virtual-tlb-and-live-ash.md), [E0449](../evidence/0449-cxd90045-ttbr1-fixmap-and-live-ash.md), [E0452](../evidence/0452-cxd90045-deferred-virtual-tlb-and-live-ash.md), [E0457](../evidence/0457-cxd90045-real-user-ttbr0-gate-and-ash.md))
- **C08** `OFFLINE` The real cause of the 'ARM decoding' symptom was host diagnostics: entry code hooks walked user page tables through a nested emu_start of an ARM MRC helper, interrupting the Thumb entry (whose first two instructions are 4-byte Thumb-2 loads, so 4-byte PC steps prove nothing). With hook-safe CP-register access and no nested emu_start, two fresh nflasha1 replays run ld.so, enter BusyBox at 0x0000C438 (USR/Thumb) and complete ash builtin roundtrips with 0 manual Thumb recoveries and identical UART bytes. ([E0533](../evidence/0533-unicorn-native-thumb-userspace-continuation.md))
- **C16** `OFFLINE` do_PrefetchAbort tracing, banked '^' hook verification, the first oops after ld-2.11.2.so, SVC-mode abort delivery, abort accounting and SWI dispatch around 0x04031AF0 were worked through. ([E0432](../evidence/0432-cxd90045-pabt-resumption-and-live-ash.md), [E0434](../evidence/0434-cxd90045-svc-dabt-and-interactive-ash.md), [E0436](../evidence/0436-cxd90045-04031af0-dispatch-and-live-ash.md))
- **C17** `OFFLINE` do_page_fault pt_regs frames, kernel-VA translation, TLB flush on ret_to_user, INTR abort re-dispatch, the SWI Thumb offset, the two kernel stacks, live SVC-stack delivery, data- vs prefetch-abort classification and an unconditional (PC, decoded VA) fault guard narrowed the 0x04031AF0 loop to a page/translation blocker. ([E0437](../evidence/0437-cxd90045-page-fault-pt-regs-and-live-ash.md), [E0438](../evidence/0438-cxd90045-tlb-flush-swi-redispatch-and-ash.md), [E0439](../evidence/0439-cxd90045-mm-fault-fix-swi-and-live-ash.md), [E0440](../evidence/0440-cxd90045-svc-stack-refresh-and-live-ash.md), [E0442](../evidence/0442-cxd90045-data-abort-classification-and-ash.md), [E0444](../evidence/0444-cxd90045-unconditional-fault-decode-and-ash.md))

### <a id="user-thumb-return"></a>User-mode return and Thumb continuation

`user.thumb-return` | process | inventory `kernel.text:ret_to_user`, `kernel.text:ret_fast_syscall`, `kernel.text:kernel_execve`

Returning to user space correctly: pt_regs frames, banked SP_usr/LR_usr, SPSR tail, Thumb state and the loader's first syscalls.

Aliases: `ret_to_user`, `ret_fast_syscall`, `0x04031AF0`, `0x0403D6B2`

- **C05** `OFFLINE` The PC=0 resume was a restore-path issue in ret_to_user; SPSR-tail capture gave the first true Thumb USR entry at 0x0402E790; generation-tagged pt_regs eliminated stale replays and ld-2.11.2.so executes deep into relocation. ([E0459](../evidence/0459-cxd90045-zero-pc-resume-and-live-ash.md), [E0461](../evidence/0461-cxd90045-pt-regs-scan-and-live-ash.md), [E0463](../evidence/0463-cxd90045-spsr-tail-restore-and-ash.md), [E0491](../evidence/0491-cxd90045-ldso-0403d6b2-and-entry-stack.md), [E0492](../evidence/0492-cxd90045-generation-tagged-ptregs-and-ldso-advance.md))
- **C06** `OFFLINE` Fixing the true user register bank, the ret_fast_syscall restore and the enforced USR|Thumb return let the first loader SVCs (brk) and the second syscall execute. ([E0494](../evidence/0494-cxd90045-usr-bank-recovery-ldso-svc-and-ash.md), [E0498](../evidence/0498-cxd90045-swi-banked-stmdb-and-live-ash.md), [E0500](../evidence/0500-cxd90045-ret-fast-syscall-usr-restore-and-ash.md), [E0503](../evidence/0503-cxd90045-ret-fast-syscall-0x6010def8-and-ash.md), [E0504](../evidence/0504-cxd90045-0x0402f666-pc-ldr-decode-fast-r0-vfp-and-busybox-entry.md))

Also: the fast-syscall frame capture clobbered the syscall return r0 (brk(0) ran twice); ld.so switches to ARM-mode helpers and __sigsetjmp's vstmia needs FPEXC.EN; kernel uaccess helpers such as __strncpy_from_user must demand-page user VAs. With these, ld.so issues uname, mmap2, access, open and stat64. ([E0504](../evidence/0504-cxd90045-0x0402f666-pc-ldr-decode-fast-r0-vfp-and-busybox-entry.md))

Do not rely on:

- ~~Unicorn's translation stays in ARM state at the ld.so entry despite CPSR.T=1 (PC steps 0x790 -> 0x794 -> 0x798), so fixed-address prologue execution, a manual Thumb stepper and forced-Thumb UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID recovery are required.~~ **R01** `RETRACTED` ([E0464](../evidence/0464-cxd90045-thumb-restore-order-and-ash.md), [E0466](../evidence/0466-cxd90045-slice-boundary-thumb-and-ash.md), [E0467](../evidence/0467-cxd90045-tb-evict-thumb-entry-and-ash.md), [E0469](../evidence/0469-cxd90045-ldso-prologue-step-and-ash.md), [E0470](../evidence/0470-cxd90045-general-thumb-stepper-and-ash.md), [E0472](../evidence/0472-cxd90045-insn-invalid-recovery-and-ash.md), [E0473](../evidence/0473-cxd90045-top-classifier-insn-recovery-and-ash.md)); see C08: The real cause of the 'ARM decoding' symptom was host diagnostics: entry code hooks walked user page tables through a nested emu_start of an ARM MRC helper, interrupting the Thumb entry (whose first two instructions are 4-byte Thumb-2 loads, so 4-byte PC steps prove nothing). With hook-safe CP-register access and no nested emu_start, two fresh nflasha1 replays run ld.so, enter BusyBox at 0x0000C438 (USR/Thumb) and complete ash builtin roundtrips with 0 manual Thumb recoveries and identical UART bytes. *Note: E0533 shows the entry is Thumb (two four-byte Thumb-2 loads then a two-byte mov) and removes those workarounds.*
- ~~The updater kernel reached first userspace: /sbin/init ran /bin/sh as PID 1, which then took a NULL-vector user exception.~~ **R05** `RETRACTED` ([E0421](../evidence/0421-cxd90045-ttyam0-uart-and-cramfs-init-boot.md)); see C34: The kernel's klog buffer (klog.addr=0x034A0000, 128 KiB) holds the real boot log. It shows console [klog0] as the only console (so nothing went to the PL011), a CRCDC timeout at 0xF2A31000, dwc3 probe -110, the cramfs root mounted read-only and then 'Failed to execute /sbin/init ... Kernel panic - not syncing: No init found' followed by Sony's exception monitor. UART0..2 resources are 0xF2000000/0xF2001000/0xF2002000. *Note: E0422: the PID-1 dump belongs to the init task panicking with 'No init found'; no user-mode instruction ran.*
- ~~The 0x04031AF0 fault is a user instruction-prefetch fault on a new page.~~ **R09** `REFUTED` ([E0437](../evidence/0437-cxd90045-page-fault-pt-regs-and-live-ash.md)); see C41: 0x04031AF0 is the Thumb load ldr r3,[r1,r0] (live bytes match ld.so offset 0x3AF0) with effective address 0x0404DF48 in ld.so's second PT_LOAD. Unicorn reports this guest translation fault as a bare UC_ERR_EXCEPTION with no unmapped-access hook, so the machine now walks TTBR0 -> L1 -> L2, decodes the instruction with capstone and delivers a data abort for the computed address (read/write by mnemonic). Unicorn also couples CPSR.T to the PC's low bit, so PC writes must keep the Thumb LSB.
